## Claims

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said there is no such thing as a duplicate content penalty.
  <br><sub>`D1-C111` · Day 1, session not recorded (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Demystifying the "duplicate content penalty"](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2008/09/demystifying-duplicate-content-penalty), [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Extended by [D2-C348](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md)</sub>

- **[Press]** As reported by Search Engine Journal, John Mueller said in April 2026 that there is no penalty or ranking demotion for having multiple URLs with the same content; Google picks one to keep.
  > "There's no penalty or ranking demotion if you have multiple URLs going to the same content."
  <br><sub>`D1-C112` · Search Engine Journal (8 April 2026) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the press report · [Google Says It Can Handle Multiple URLs To The Same Content](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-says-it-can-handle-multiple-urls-to-the-same-content/571424/)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonicalization guide says some duplicate content on a site is normal and not a violation of its spam policies; Google clusters duplicate pages, picks the most representative one as canonical and crawls the duplicates less often.
  > "Some duplicate content on a site is normal and it's not a violation of Google's spam policies."
  <br><sub>`D1-C128` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Repeated by [D1-C207](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C031](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Extended by [D2-C345](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C369](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C408](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Extended by [D2-C701](D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) · Used by the glossary term *Duplicate cluster*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The real cost of duplicates is control and crawling: Google may choose a canonical you did not want, and every copy is still crawled. Copied or scraped content is a separate spam-policy issue.
  <br><sub>`D1-C113` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · Extended by [D2-C380](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C401](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's crawlers do not click buttons. Each page in a series needs its own URL and an `<a href>` link to the next page, should not use page 1 as its canonical, and rel=next and rel=prev are no longer used.
  <br><sub>`D1-C115` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Repeated by [D2-C040](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Extended by [D2-C184](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C187](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C195](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C201](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C268](D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C276](D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Contradicted by [D2-C393](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C395](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

  <br><sub>`D1-C118` · Day 1, session not recorded · consistent with Google docs · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Extended by [D1-C279](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-04`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide for generative AI features says browser agents may read a site through screenshots, the DOM structure and the accessibility tree, and recommends semantic HTML because it helps users such as screen reader users navigate a page.
  <br><sub>`D1-C131` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Repeated by [D1-C274](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Extended by [D1-C278](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C397](D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C465](D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google has not called ARIA a ranking signal. The case for it is that AI agents and assistive tools read pages through the same structure: real buttons, labelled forms and semantic headings.

- **[Stage]** Speakers at the event were openly dismissive of llms.txt.
  <br><sub>`D1-C060` · Day 1, session not recorded · Extended by [D1-C271](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Googlebot does not support HTTP/3 today.
  <br><sub>`D1-C075` · Day 1, session not recorded · consistent with Google docs · [Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers (user agents)](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/overview-google-crawlers) · Used by `DEV-SRV-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's crawlers support HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, use whichever gives the best crawling performance, and may switch between sessions. HTTP/2 can save server resources but gives no ranking benefit.
  <br><sub>`D1-C076` · Google · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers (user agents)](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/overview-google-crawlers) · Used by `DEV-SRV-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** This does not mean avoiding HTTP/3, which benefits browsers. The rule is never to run a host that only answers over HTTP/3, and to check that CDN or firewall rules written for HTTP/3 traffic do not break HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
  <br><sub>`D1-C077` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · Used by `DEV-SRV-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's crawler overview says HTTP/1.1 is the default protocol of Google's crawlers and that a site can opt out of crawling over HTTP/2 by answering Google's HTTP/2 requests with a 421 status code.
  <br><sub>`D1-C139` · Google · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers (user agents)](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/overview-google-crawlers) · Used by `DEV-SRV-07`</sub>
